mainTopic: How ארץ ישראל was divided: was it given to יוצאי מצרים (those who left Egypt) or to באי הארץ (those who actually entered the land)?
overview: The גמרא opens by noting that our משנה follows the view that ארץ ישראל was divided among יוצאי מצרים, the people who left Egypt. It then brings a ברייתא that records a debate on this question. רבי יאשיה says the land went to those who left Egypt. He reads the other פסוק, 'לָאֵלֶּה', as 'כָּאֵלֶּה', meaning only adults like those counted, so young children are left out. רבי יונתן says the land went to באי הארץ, the people who entered it. He explains the 'fathers' פסוק as describing an unusual inheritance in which 'the dead inherit from the living.' רבי gives a parable about two brothers who are כהנים: they collect shares by the number of their sons, then bring everything back to their father and split it equally. The ברייתא then introduces a third opinion, from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Our משנה follows the view that the land went to those who left Egypt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the משנה matches the opinion that ארץ ישראל was divided among יוצאי מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה we learned follows the opinion that the land was divided among the people who left Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is labeling our משנה: it fits one side of a known debate. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave portions to people like צלפחד and חפר, who left Egypt but did not enter the land. That only makes sense if the land was divided based on the generation that left Egypt. The גמרא now needs to show where this opinion comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
In line with the one who says

phrases.english: Gemara
We learned in accordance with the one who says
the land was divided among those who left Egypt

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows the view that ארץ ישראל was divided among יוצאי מצרים.

steps.title: Rabbi Yoshiya: the land was divided among those who left Egypt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the source: רבי יאשיה learns from a פסוק that the land went to יוצאי מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יאשיה says the land was divided among those who left Egypt, because the פסוק says, 'According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show who holds the opinion it just mentioned. רבי יאשיה gives a פסוק for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the tribes of their fathers' point to the fathers, meaning the generation that left Egypt. So the shares are counted according to that older generation.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
As it is said (in a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yoshiya says:
The land was divided among those who left Egypt,
as it is said: "According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion that step 1 says our משנה follows.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that the land was divided among יוצאי מצרים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יאשיה, based on 'לִשְׁמוֹת מַטּוֹת אֲבֹתָם יִנְחָלוּ'.

steps.title: Rabbi Yoshiya faces the other verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה asks himself how he explains the פסוק 'To these the land shall be divided,' which seems to point to the people who entered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק, 'To these the land shall be divided as an inheritance'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה raises a challenge against his own view. He is setting up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'These' refers to the people who had just been counted in the wilderness, the generation about to enter the land. That sounds like the opposite of רבי יאשיה's view, so he must explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: But how do I explain (fulfill) this פסוק?

phrases.english: But how do I fulfill
"To these the land shall be divided as an inheritance"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 26:53. 'These' are the people just counted in the wilderness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יאשיה's view from a second פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יאשיה's claim that the land went to יוצאי מצרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'To these' seems to give the land to the counted generation that entered the land.

steps.title: 'To these' means 'like these,' excluding young children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה reads 'לָאֵלֶּה' as 'כָּאֵלֶּה': only people like those counted get a share, which excludes the children.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To these' means 'like these,' to exclude the young children.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה answers his own challenge by reading the word a little differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not read 'these' as the group that receives the land. He reads it as describing what kind of person gets a share: people like those counted, who were adults. This keeps the land with the generation that left Egypt, and teaches that people who were young children at the time get no share of their own.

phrases.english: "To these" means like these,
phrases.notes: Like the people counted, who were over twenty.

phrases.english: to exclude the young children.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'like these' means the land goes to the new generation. For רבי יאשיה, it only describes who counts, namely adults, and the shares still follow the generation that left Egypt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'To these' names the generation entering the land as the receivers.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'To these' describes a type (adults like those counted) and excludes young children.

steps.title: Rabbi Yonatan: the land was divided among those who entered it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן holds the opposite view: the land went to באי הארץ, based on 'To these the land shall be divided.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: the land was divided among those who entered the land, as the פסוק says, 'To these the land shall be divided as an inheritance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the second opinion, which disagrees with רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן takes 'To these' simply: the generation that was counted and entered the land is the one that receives it. The very פסוק רבי יאשיה had to explain is his main proof.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says:
The land was divided among those who entered the land,
as it is said: "To these the land shall be divided as an inheritance."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opinion that disagrees with רבי יאשיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The land was divided among באי הארץ.

steps.title: Rabbi Yonatan faces the 'fathers' verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן asks how he explains 'According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק, 'According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי יונתן faces רבי יאשיה's פסוק. He is setting up his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק mentions the fathers, which sounds like the generation that left Egypt. רבי יונתן has to show how it fits his view.

phrases.english: But how do I fulfill
"According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 3, now challenging רבי יונתן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן's claim that the land went to באי הארץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק links the inheritance to 'their fathers,' who were the generation that left Egypt.

steps.title: An unusual inheritance: the dead inherit from the living
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that this inheritance is unusual. Normally the living inherit from the dead, but here the dead inherit from the living.
steps.simpleTranslation: This inheritance is different from every other inheritance in the world. In all other inheritances, the living inherit from the dead, but here the dead inherit from the living.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן explains the 'fathers' פסוק by describing a reverse kind of inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those entering the land receive the portions, but the portions are then counted as passing to their dead fathers, and back down from them. So both פסוקים are true: the living receive the land, and the fathers' names decide the final split.

keyTerms.meaning: The living inherit from the dead
The dead inherit from the living

phrases.english: This inheritance is unusual
compared to all inheritances in the world;
for in all inheritances in the world,
the living inherit from the dead,
but here, the dead inherit from the living.
phrases.notes: The land first goes 'up' to the fathers who left מצרים, then comes back down from them.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יאשיה: the land went to יוצאי מצרים, and 'לָאֵלֶּה' only excludes children. רבי יונתן: the land went to באי הארץ, but it passed up to the dead fathers and back down ('the dead inherit from the living').
steps.triggerLanguage: מְשׁוּנָּה נַחֲלָה זוֹ מִכׇּל נְחָלוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק as teaching a special inheritance process
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Their fathers' means the land was given to the generation that left Egypt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The entering generation receives the land, but it passes up to the dead fathers and is divided again from them.

steps.title: רבי's parable: two brothers who are kohanim
steps.stepSummary: רבי begins a parable about two brothers who are כהנים, one with one son and one with two sons, whose sons go to the threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: I will give you a parable. What is this like? Two brothers who are כהנים live in one town. One has one son, and the other has two sons, and they went to the threshing floor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי starts a parable to make 'the dead inherit from the living' easier to picture. This step sets up the story, and the next step finishes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons stand for the generation entering the land, and the brothers stand for the fathers who left Egypt. At the threshing floor each כהן collects one share of תרומה, so the number of sons decides how much each family collects at first.

keyTerms.meaning: I will give you a parable
Threshing floor, where תרומה is given out

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
I will give you a parable,
to what is the matter similar?
To two brothers who are priests
who were in one town,
one has one son,
and one has two sons,
and they went to the threshing floor.
phrases.notes: They went to collect תרומה, which is given out one share per כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבי יונתן's idea of 'the dead inherit from the living.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A parable is introduced to explain the double-step division of the land.

steps.title: Collect by sons, then redivide equally between the brothers
steps.stepSummary: Each brother first takes shares by his number of sons. Then everything goes back to their father and is divided again equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: The brother with one son takes one share, and the brother with two sons takes two shares. They bring it all back to their father, and then they divide it again equally.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי finishes the parable and shows the two stages of the division.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stage one: shares are collected by the living sons (1 and 2, so 3 in total). Stage two: everything goes back to the father and is split equally between the brothers, one and a half each. In the same way, the land was counted by those entering it, then passed up to the fathers and divided again by the fathers' line.

phrases.english: This one who has one son
takes one portion,
and that one who has two sons
takes two portions.
And they bring them back to their father,
phrases.notes: 'Their father' is the two brothers' own father, the boys' grandfather.

phrases.english: and they go back and divide equally.

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the roles straight: the sons stand for those entering the land, and the brothers stand for the fathers who left מצרים. The final equal split follows the brothers, not the number of sons.
steps.whyThisMatters: This picture of 'counted by the living, divided by the dead' is how רבי יונתן makes both פסוקים work together.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the parable begun in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shares are first collected by the number of living sons, then returned to the father and redivided equally between his sons.

steps.title: A third opinion begins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא introduces רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who is about to give a third view on how the land was divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It names a new speaker, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, but his actual statement comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we saw two opposite views about who received the land: the people who left מצרים, or the people who entered the land (רבי יונתן's view). Bringing in a third תנא tells us his view will likely be a different approach to the same question. For now, all we know is who is speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, and the third voice in this ברייתא about dividing the land
Says. This word introduces a תנא's opinion
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה. This discussion is part of one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's opinion in this line. It is only the introduction, and his actual words come next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יונתן finished his view and the parable of the two brothers, the ברייתא turns to a third תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not stated yet. This line only introduces רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and his ruling follows.
